draft.title: Where the world's water is
card: Most of the Earth's water is salt water in the oceans. Only a small share is fresh water, which has very little salt.
Most fresh water is not easy to use. A large part is frozen in ice sheets and glaciers, and much of the rest is stored underground.
Only a tiny share of the world's fresh water is in rivers, lakes and wetlands, where people can reach it most easily.
So the water that people can easily reach is a very small part of all the water on Earth.
draft.remember: Most water is salty ocean, and most fresh water is frozen or underground, so easy-to-reach water is scarce.

a.q: Which statement about the Earth's water is correct?
opts: Most of it is salt water in the oceans
Most of it is fresh water in rivers and lakes
Most of it is fresh water stored in the ground
Most of it is fresh water frozen in glaciers
a.why: Most of the Earth's water is salty ocean. Fresh water is only a small share of the total, so the options about fresh water cannot describe most of the Earth's water, even though a lot of fresh water is frozen or underground.
a.clue: Think about how much of the Earth's water is salty compared with fresh.

b.q: A student says, "Most of the world's fresh water is in rivers and lakes, so it is easy to reach." Why is the student wrong?
opts: Most fresh water is frozen or stored underground
Most fresh water is in the oceans, mixed with salt
Most fresh water is in rivers, but it is too polluted
Most fresh water is in the clouds, as water vapour
b.why: Most fresh water is locked in ice or held underground, and only a tiny share is in rivers and lakes. The ocean option is wrong because ocean water is salty, so it is not fresh water.
b.clue: Where is most fresh water kept, and is it easy to reach?

a.best: Most of it is salt water in the oceans

b.best: Most fresh water is frozen or stored underground
